subject: Zoology
stem: The number of vertebrae in a human is ______.
solution: The vertebral column is formed by 26 serially arranged vertebrae: 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 1 sacral (fused) and 1 coccygeal (fused). Seven is the cervical count, 12 the thoracic count and 206 the bones of the whole skeleton. So the answer is option C.

subject: Botany
stem: Symbiotic association between fungi and algae are called ______.
solution: Lichens are symbiotic, mutually useful associations between algae and fungi: the algal partner (phycobiont) makes food, and the fungal partner (mycobiont) gives shelter and absorbs mineral nutrients and water. Mycorrhiza is an association of fungi with the roots of higher plants, sponges are animals, and chrysophytes are a group of protists. So option A.

subject: Botany
subtopic: Cell Theory and the Prokaryotic Cell
stem: Cell theory was formulated by ______.
solution: Matthias Schleiden, a botanist, and Theodore Schwann, a zoologist, together formulated the cell theory (1838 to 1839). Robert Brown discovered the nucleus, Singer and Nicolson proposed the fluid mosaic model of the membrane, and Antonie von Leeuwenhoek first saw and described a live cell. So option A.

subject: Botany
subtopic: Cell Theory and the Prokaryotic Cell
stem:
Which of the following are characteristics of prokaryotic cells ?
(a) Ribosomes are made of 50S and 30S subunits
(b) They can have plasmids
(c) They contain mesosome
(d) They have peroxisomes
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution: Prokaryotes have 70S ribosomes made of a 50S and a 30S subunit (a), many bacteria carry small circular plasmids outside the genomic DNA (b), and their plasma membrane forms infoldings called mesosomes (c). Prokaryotes have no membrane-bound organelles, so they lack peroxisomes (d). So (a), (b) and (c) only, option D.

subject: Zoology
stem: Which of the following is not a part of human central neural system ?
solution: Inside the skull the brain is covered by the cranial meninges: an outer dura mater, a very thin middle arachnoid and an inner pia mater in contact with the brain tissue. These are coverings of the central neural system. The pericardium is the double-walled bag that protects the heart, so it is not a part of the central neural system. So the answer is option D.

subject: Botany
stem: Mitochondrial inner membrane encloses ______.
solution: The mitochondrion has two membranes that divide its lumen into two aqueous compartments. The inner membrane, folded into cristae, encloses the inner compartment, which is filled with a dense homogeneous substance called the matrix. Cytosol is the fluid of the cell outside the organelles, and mucus and aqueous humour are not parts of a mitochondrion. So option A.

subject: Botany
stem:
Match List-I with List-II.

| List-I | List-II |
|---|---|
| A. Cristae | I. Flat membrane sacs in stroma of chloroplast |
| B. Cisternae | II. Infoldings in mitochondria |
| C. Thylakoids | III. Cell membrane |
| D. Phospholipid | IV. Disc shaped sacs in the Golgi apparatus |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution: Cristae are the infoldings of the inner mitochondrial membrane (A-II). Cisternae are the flat, disc-shaped sacs of the Golgi apparatus (B-IV). Thylakoids are the flat membranous sacs in the stroma of the chloroplast (C-I). Phospholipids, arranged in a bilayer, are the main lipids of the cell membrane (D-III). So option B.

subject: Botany
stem: The plastid that stores xanthophyll is known as ______.
solution: Chromoplasts contain fat-soluble carotenoid pigments such as carotene and xanthophylls, which give parts of the plant yellow, orange or red colours. Chloroplasts mainly hold chlorophyll, while aleuroplasts (which store proteins) and amyloplasts (which store starch) are colourless leucoplasts. So option B.

subject: Zoology
stem:
Which of the following statements related to pituitary gland are correct ?
(a) It is divided anatomically into adenohypophysis and neurohypophysis
(b) It secretes follicle stimulating hormone
(c) It secretes melanocyte stimulating hormone
(d) It does not secrete prolactin
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution: The pituitary is divided anatomically into an adenohypophysis and a neurohypophysis, so (a) is true. The pars distalis secretes GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH and FSH, so (b) is true and (d) is false, since prolactin is a pars distalis hormone. The pars intermedia secretes MSH, so (c) is true. So (a), (b) and (c) only. So the answer is option B.

subject: Botany
stem:
Photorespiration reaction catalyzed by RuBisCo is shown below :
\(\text{RuBP} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{3-Phosphoglycerate} + X\)
Identify "X" from the given options :
solution: When RuBisCO binds \(O_2\) instead of \(CO_2\), RuBP gives one molecule of phosphoglycerate (3 carbons) and one molecule of phosphoglycolate (2 carbons). So X is 2-phosphoglycolate. Phosphoenolpyruvate, oxaloacetate and malate belong to the C4 pathway, not to this reaction. So option B.

subject: Botany
stem: Mad cow disease is caused by ______.
solution: Prions are infectious agents made of abnormally folded protein, similar in size to viruses. They cause bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), commonly called mad cow disease, in cattle and its analogue, Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD), in humans. Viroids are free RNA that cause potato spindle tuber disease, and Aspergillus and Mycoplasma do not cause BSE. So option A.

subject: Botany
stem: Which pigment has absorption peak at 700 nm in the photosynthetic reaction centre PS I (P700) ?
solution: In each photosystem all the pigments form a light-harvesting antenna except one molecule of chlorophyll a, which forms the reaction centre. In PS I this chlorophyll a has its absorption peak at 700 nm and is called P700 (in PS II it is P680). Chlorophyll b, xanthophylls and carotenoids are accessory pigments that pass the absorbed energy on. So option B.

subject: Zoology
stem: In water, frogs respire using ______.
solution: In water, the frog's skin acts as the respiratory organ (cutaneous respiration): dissolved oxygen is exchanged through the skin by diffusion. On land the buccal cavity, the skin and the lungs all act as respiratory organs. So the answer is option A.

subject: Zoology
stem: Which of the following represents the correct sequence of arrangement of bones in the lower limb of humans ?
solution: The lower limb has the femur (thigh bone), then the patella, a cup-shaped bone covering the knee ventrally, then the tibia and fibula, then the tarsals of the ankle. So the order is femur, patella, tibia, tarsal. So the answer is option C.

subject: Botany
stem: Phyllotaxy is the pattern of arrangement of ______.
solution: Phyllotaxy is the pattern in which leaves are arranged on the stem or branch. It is usually of three types: alternate (china rose, mustard, sunflower), opposite (Calotropis, guava) and whorled (Alstonia). The arrangement of flowers on the floral axis is the inflorescence, and the arrangement of sepals or petals in a bud is aestivation. So option A.

subject: Zoology
stem:
Match List-I with List-II

| List-I | List-II |
|---|---|
| A. Starch | I. Fights infection |
| B. Antibody | II. Energy storage |
| C. Concanavalin | III. Glucose transport |
| D. Glut-4 | IV. Lectin |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution: Starch is the store of energy in plant tissues (A-II). Antibodies fight infectious agents (B-I). Concanavalin A is a lectin (C-IV). GLUT-4 enables glucose transport into cells (D-III). So option B.

subject: Zoology
stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called radial symmetry.
Statement II : In phylum Echinodermata, both adults and larvae are radially symmetrical.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
solution: Statement I is NCERT's description of radial symmetry, so it is correct. Statement II is incorrect: adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical, but their larvae are bilaterally symmetrical. So the answer is option C.

subject: Botany
stem: Endomembrane system includes ______.
options: endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuole
endoplasmic reticulum, chloroplast, peroxisomes and vacuole
Golgi complex, chloroplast, peroxisomes and vacuole
solution: The endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles form the endomembrane system, because their functions are coordinated. Mitochondria, chloroplasts and peroxisomes are not part of it, since their functions are not coordinated with these organelles. Option A is the only choice without one of these. So option A.

subject: Botany
stem: How many molecules of pyruvic acid are produced at the end of glycolysis from 206 molecules of glucose ?
solution: NCERT-XI-156. 2 molecules of pyruvic acid are produced at the end of glycolysis from 1 molecule of glucose. So 206 molecules of glucose will produce \(\Rightarrow 206 \times 2 = 412\) molecules of pyruvic acid

subject: Botany
stem: Which of the following plant growth regulators is used as herbicide ?
solution: 2,4-D, a synthetic auxin, is widely used as a herbicide to kill dicotyledonous weeds; it does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants, so gardeners use it to prepare weed-free lawns. Kinetin is a cytokinin, abscisic acid is a growth inhibitor and gibberellin is a growth promoter; none of them is used as a weedkiller. So option A.

subject: Botany
stem:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : In gymnosperms, the male and female gametophytes remain within the sporangia.
Statement II : In gymnosperms, seeds are not covered.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
solution: Both statements are correct. Unlike bryophytes and pteridophytes, the male and female gametophytes of gymnosperms have no independent free-living existence: they remain within the sporangia retained on the sporophyte. The ovules are not enclosed by an ovary wall, so the seeds that develop after fertilisation are not covered (naked seeds). So option A.

subject: Botany
stem:
Match List-I with List-II.

| List-I | List-II |
|---|---|
| A. Spherical | I. Vibrio |
| B. Rod | II. Cocci |
| C. Comma | III. Spirilla |
| D. Spirillum | IV. Bacilli |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution: Bacteria are grouped by shape: spherical bacteria are cocci (A-II), rod-shaped bacteria are bacilli (B-IV), comma-shaped bacteria are vibrio (C-I) and spiral bacteria are spirilla (D-III). So option D.

subject: Botany
stem:
Which of the following are characteristic features of Solanaceae family ?
(a) Flowers are bisexual and actinomorphic
(b) Calyx have five sepals and are united
(c) Androecium have five stamens and are epipetalous
(d) Ovary is inferior
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution: In Solanaceae the flowers are bisexual and actinomorphic (a), the calyx has five united sepals (b), and the five stamens are epipetalous (c). The ovary is superior, bicarpellary and syncarpous, not inferior, so (d) is false. So (a), (b) and (c) only, option A.

subject: Botany
stem: Select the correct sequence of experiments that led to a gradual understanding of photosynthesis in green plants.
options: Absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b \(\rightarrow\) production of glucose \(\rightarrow\) release of oxygen \(\rightarrow\) role of air
Role of air \(\rightarrow\) release of oxygen \(\rightarrow\) production of glucose \(\rightarrow\) absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b
Release of oxygen \(\rightarrow\) production of glucose \(\rightarrow\) absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b \(\rightarrow\) role of air
Production of glucose \(\rightarrow\) role of air \(\rightarrow\) release of oxygen \(\rightarrow\) absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b
solution: Priestley (1770) showed that plants restore the air that a burning candle or a breathing animal spoils, which established the role of air. Ingenhousz then showed that sunlight is needed and that only the green parts of plants release oxygen. Julius von Sachs (1854) showed that the green parts make glucose, usually stored as starch. Later Engelmann found that the action spectrum of photosynthesis roughly resembles the absorption spectra of chlorophyll a and b. So the order is role of air, release of oxygen, production of glucose, absorption spectra: option B.

subject: Zoology
stem: The number of action potentials generated by sino-arterial node (SAN) in a healthy human is ________ per minute.
solution: The nodal musculature can generate action potentials without any external stimulus (it is autoexcitable). The SA node generates the most action potentials, about 70 to 75 a minute, so it starts and maintains the rhythm of the heart and is called the pacemaker. The normal heart rate is 72 beats a minute. So the answer is option B.

subject: Botany
stem: How many turns of Calvin cycle are required for the formation of three molecules of glucose ?
solution: NCERT-XI-144. For the formation of 1 molecule of glucose 6 turns of calvin cycle are required. So for the formation of 3 molecules of glucose \(\Rightarrow 3 \times 6 = 18\) turns of calvin cycle are required

subject: Zoology
stem: Which of the following statements is incorrect ?
options: Blood coagulates in response to an injury
solution: Blood coagulates in response to an injury. The clot is a network of fibrin threads, and fibrin is formed from the inactive plasma protein fibrinogen by the enzyme thrombin. So the statement that fibrinogen is produced from fibrin reverses the order and is the incorrect one. So the answer is option D.

subject: Botany
stem:
Match List-I with List-II.

| List-I | List-II |
|---|---|
| A. Family | I. Sapindales |
| B. Genus | II. Dicotyledonae |
| C. Class | III. Anacardiaceae |
| D. Phylum | IV. Angiospermae |
| E. Order | V. Mangifera |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution: NCERT's table of organisms with their taxonomic categories places mango (Mangifera indica) in genus Mangifera, family Anacardiaceae, order Sapindales, class Dicotyledonae and division Angiospermae. So family is Anacardiaceae (A-III), genus is Mangifera (B-V), class is Dicotyledonae (C-II), phylum is Angiospermae (D-IV) and order is Sapindales (E-I). So option D.

subject: Botany
stem:
Arrange the following taxonomic categories in ascending order.
(a) Genus
(b) Class
(c) Order
(d) Phylum
(e) Family
(f) Kingdom
(g) Species
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution: Ascending order runs from the lowest category to the highest: species (g), genus (a), family (e), order (c), class (b), phylum (d) and kingdom (f). Only option A follows this sequence; the other options mix up the ranks. So option A.

subject: Botany
stem:
Match List-I with List-II.

| List-I | List-II |
|---|---|
| A. Marginal placentation | I. Argemone |
| B. Axile placentation | II. Tomato |
| C. Parietal placentation | III. Primrose |
| D. Free central placentation | IV. Pea |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution: In marginal placentation the placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture of the ovary, as in pea (A-IV). In axile placentation the ovules are attached to a central placenta in a multilocular ovary, as in tomato (B-II). In parietal placentation the ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary, as in Argemone (C-I). In free central placentation the ovules are borne on a central axis without septa, as in primrose (D-III). So option D.

subject: Botany
stem: Sphenopsida class belongs to ________ .
solution: Pteridophytes are divided into four classes: Psilopsida (Psilotum), Lycopsida (Selaginella, Lycopodium), Sphenopsida (Equisetum) and Pteropsida (Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum). So Sphenopsida is a class of pteridophytes, option D.

subject: Botany
stem:
Which of the following statements regarding photorespiration are correct ?
(a) Do not occur in C3 plants
(b) \(\text{CO}_2\) is consumed and \(\text{O}_2\) is generated
(c) Phosphoglycolate is formed
(d) No synthesis of ATP and NADPH
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution: (a) is wrong: photorespiration occurs in C3 plants; it is C4 plants in which it does not occur. (b) is wrong: in photorespiration \(O_2\) is used and \(CO_2\) is released. (c) is right: RuBisCO binds \(O_2\), and RuBP gives one molecule of phosphoglycerate and one of phosphoglycolate. (d) is right: photorespiration makes no sugar and no ATP or NADPH; rather it releases \(CO_2\) and uses up ATP. So (c) and (d) only, option B.

subject: Botany
stem: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum ________ .
options: has ribosomes attached to its surface
is the major site for the synthesis of lipids
is actively involved in protein synthesis
is a site for the synthesis of carbohydrates
solution: The smooth endoplasmic reticulum has no ribosomes on its surface and is the major site of lipid synthesis; in animal cells it also makes lipid-like steroidal hormones. Ribosomes on the surface and active protein synthesis are features of the rough endoplasmic reticulum, and carbohydrate synthesis is not the role NCERT gives the smooth ER. So option B.

subject: Zoology
stem: Which one of the following statements is incorrect ?
solution: In the islets of Langerhans, the alpha cells secrete glucagon and the beta cells secrete insulin. Glucagon stimulates glycogenolysis in the liver. So the statement that alpha cells secrete insulin is the incorrect one. So the answer is option B.

subject: Botany
stem: Genus represents ________ .
options: a population of plants and animals
a group of closely related species
a group of closely related families
solution: A genus is a group of closely related species that share more characters with each other than with species of other genera; lion, leopard and tiger, for example, are species of the genus Panthera. An individual plant or animal is a single organism, and a population is a group of individuals of one species. A group of closely related families is an order, not a genus. So option C.

subject: Botany
stem: Which of the following is not a prokaryote ?
solution: Kingdom Monera is the only kingdom of prokaryotes; it includes bacteria, cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) and mycoplasma, which have no membrane-bound nucleus. Fungi have a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles, so they are eukaryotes. So option D.

subject: Botany
stem: Which of the following plant growth regulators promotes internode elongation prior to flowering in cabbage ?
solution: Gibberellins promote bolting, the internode elongation just before flowering, in beet, cabbage and many plants with a rosette habit. Abscisic acid is a growth inhibitor, indole butyric acid is an auxin known for initiating roots on stem cuttings, and ethephon releases ethylene. So option B.

subject: Botany
stem: The correct sequence of adult cell cycle phases is ______ .
solution: Interphase comes first, in the order \(G_1\) phase (the cell grows but does not replicate its DNA), S phase (DNA replication) and \(G_2\) phase (proteins are made in preparation for mitosis). M phase, the actual division, follows interphase. So the sequence is \(G_1\), S, \(G_2\), M, option C.

subject: Botany
stem:
Match List-I with List-II.

| List-I | List-II |
|---|---|
| A. Fusion of protoplasms between gametes | I. Meiosis |
| B. Fusion of two nuclei | II. Plasmogamy |
| C. Generation of haploid spores | III. Karyogamy |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution: The sexual cycle of fungi has three steps: fusion of the protoplasms of two gametes is plasmogamy (A-II), fusion of two nuclei is karyogamy (B-III), and meiosis in the zygote gives haploid spores (C-I). So option A.

subject: Zoology
stem:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The class name Reptilia refers to creeping or crawling mode of locomotion.
Statement II : All organisms belonging to Reptilia have three chambered heart.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
solution: Statement I is correct: NCERT says the name Reptilia refers to their creeping or crawling mode of locomotion. Statement II is incorrect: the reptile heart is usually three-chambered, but crocodiles have a four-chambered heart. So the answer is option C.

subject: Botany
stem:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Chromosomes are fully condensed at the end of prophase I.
Statement II : Meiosis I resembles mitosis.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is true
solution: Statement I is correct: by diakinesis, the last stage of prophase I, the chromosomes are fully condensed and the meiotic spindle is assembled. Statement II is false: it is meiosis II that resembles a normal mitosis, whereas meiosis I pairs the homologous chromosomes and separates them, halving the chromosome number. So option C.

subject: Zoology
stem: Which of the following is not a characteristic of chordates ?
solution: Chordates have a notochord, a dorsal hollow nerve cord, paired pharyngeal gill slits and a post-anal tail. Absence of gill slits is a feature of non-chordates, so it is not a characteristic of chordates. So the answer is option C.

subject: Botany
stem: Length of the stem at time 0 is 20 cm. The arithmetic growth rate is 30 cm per day. What is the length of the stem at the end of the 7\(^\text{th}\) day ?
solution: NCERT-XI-170. For arithmetic growth \(\Rightarrow L_t = L_0 + rt\). \(L_t = ?\) ; \(L_0 = 20\) cm ; \(r = 30\) cm/day ; \(t = 7\) days. So \(L_t = 20 + 30 \times 7 = 20 + 210 = 230\) cm

subject: Zoology
stem:
Arrange the following elements in descending order of their contribution to percentage weight of the human body.
(a) Oxygen
(b) Carbon
(c) Hydrogen
(d) Nitrogen
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution:
**Note:** NCERT's table of elements gives hydrogen as only 0.5 per cent of body weight, which would put nitrogen (3.3 per cent) above hydrogen; no option has that order. By the usual figures for the human body, hydrogen is about 10 per cent, which gives oxygen, carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, the paper's key.

Oxygen is the largest share of body weight (about 65 per cent) and carbon the next (about 18.5 per cent). Hydrogen and nitrogen follow. So the answer is option A.

subject: Zoology
stem: In frogs, the number of pairs of cranial nerves arising from the brain are ______ .
solution: NCERT says that in the frog, ten pairs of cranial nerves arise from the brain. So the answer is option C.
